Settler colonialism is a process by which settlers exercise colonial rule over a land and its indigenous peoples , transforming the land and replacing or assimilating its population with or into the society of the settlers. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] Assimilation has sometimes been conceptualized in biological terms such as the "breeding of a minority population into a majority," but in other cases, such as in some parts of Latin America , biological mixing of populations was less problematic. [ 6 ]
